did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm is attributed to the sons of Korah, and it opens by describing the foundations of a holy place: the holy mountains.
Did you know? The psalm emphasizes that the LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob, presenting Zion as a place of special status.
Did you know? Zion is called here “the city of God,” and glorious things are spoken about it; the word “Selah” closes the verse and emphasizes its importance.
Did you know? The psalm mentions Rahab, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Cush together, presenting them all in connection with birth and recognition associated with the place.
Did you know? The expression “each and every one” emphasizes that every person born in Zion is included in the praise, not just one unique or exceptional figure.
Did you know? It is said of Zion that the LORD himself will establish it, so the psalm presents its status as dependent on divine foundation.
Did you know? The psalm describes the LORD as counting the nations in a register, and within that record he declares: “This one was born there.”
Did you know? At the end, singers and dancers are described, and the speaker says, “All my springs are in you”—a poetic expression centering his sources or aspirations in Zion.
